timeline.label: Completed acquisition of Calpine, adding natural-gas generation and ERCOT exposure; Q1 2026 investing cash outflow included $2.5B net for Calpine
Executed 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft to restart Three Mile Island Unit 1 as Crane Clean Energy Center (~835 MW emissions-free capacity when operational)
FY2025 normalized owner cash was $1.29B ($3.57/sh) after $2.95B capital spending on a $4.24B operating cash flow base
FY2025 revenue reached $25.5B; net income $2.32B versus $3.75B prior year as merchant and cost dynamics shifted
Acquired 44% undivided interest in South Texas Project (2,645 MW nuclear); consideration $1.66B
Spun out of Exelon as standalone Constellation Energy; focus on competitive generation and retail supply

industry.structure: US competitive power is consolidating around large fleets that can serve regulated utilities, wholesale markets (PJM, ERCOT, etc.), and increasingly data-center buyers seeking 24/7 clean power. Nuclear operators hold scarce baseload licenses; gas plants add dispatch flexibility. Retail supply adds customer relationships but thin margins.
industry.share_shift: CEG is gaining scale via Calpine and nuclear restarts/partnerships while hyperscalers sign long-dated PPAs directly with generators, bypassing traditional utility intermediaries for firm power.
industry.trend: AI and data-center build-out is raising demand for reliable around-the-clock electricity; nuclear restart economics improve with long-term corporate PPAs (Microsoft at Crane). Debt-funded M&A and heavy capital spending keep normalized owner cash well below headline revenue growth.
